header.userPrompt:
Fix an infinite recursion bug in the ZIO 1 stubbing helpers.

File: effects/zio1/src/main/scala/sttp/client4/impl/zio/SttpClientStubbingBase.scala

`AbstractClientStubbing` defines `val monad = new RIOMonadAsyncError[R]` (line ~20). In `StreamClientStubbing.proxy` (line ~101) and `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing.proxy` (line ~120), the anonymous backend classes define `def monad: MonadError[RIO[R, *]] = monad`. Inside the anonymous class, `monad` resolves to the method itself, so calling `monad` on the proxied backend recurses forever (StackOverflowError).

Acceptance criteria:
1. Both proxy backends' `monad` return the outer trait's `RIOMonadAsyncError` instance (e.g. via a self-alias or a qualified reference such as `AbstractClientStubbing.this.monad` / a local val captured before the anonymous class). Pick the simplest, clearest form.
2. Check whether the ZIO 2 module (effects/zio/...) has the same pattern; fix it there too if so.
3. Add a regression test in the zio1 module's test sources (follow existing test layout) that calls `monad` on the proxied backend (both stream and websocket-stream variants) and verifies it does not recurse and returns a usable MonadError.
4. Compile and run the relevant tests, e.g. `sbt "testScoped 3 JVM"` scoped to the zio1 project (find the exact project id in build.sbt, e.g. `zio1JVM/test` / `zio1/test`), and for Scala 2.13 as well.

Keep the change minimal.

resultJson.description:
In the ZIO 1 stubbing helpers (`effects/zio1/.../SttpClientStubbingBase.scala`), the anonymous backends created by `StreamClientStubbing.proxy` and `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing.proxy` define `def monad: MonadError[RIO[R, *]] = monad`. Inside the anonymous class `monad` refers to the method itself, so any call to `monad` on the proxied backend (e.g. the one provided by `HttpClientZioBackend.stubLayer` or armeria-zio1's `SttpClientStubbing.layer`) overflows the stack.

The fix makes both proxies return the enclosing trait's `RIOMonadAsyncError[R]` instance through a qualified reference (`StreamClientStubbing.this.monad` / `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing.this.monad`), and adds a regression test covering both variants.

The ZIO 2 module (`effects/zio`) was checked: it has no `SttpClientStubbingBase.scala` and no `*ClientStubbing` traits, and a repo-wide search for `def monad ... = monad` finds only the two zio1 lines. Nothing to change there.

tasks.title: Fix self-recursive `monad` in zio1 stubbing proxies and add a regression test
tasks.description:
In `effects/zio1/src/main/scala/sttp/client4/impl/zio/SttpClientStubbingBase.scala` change the two anonymous-backend definitions (line 101 in `StreamClientStubbing.proxy`, line 120 in `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing.proxy`) from `def monad: MonadError[RIO[R, *]] = monad` to a qualified outer reference: `StreamClientStubbing.this.monad` and `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing.this.monad` respectively. Change nothing else (keep the public `val monad = new RIOMonadAsyncError[R]` and its inferred type as is).

Add a regression test `effects/zio1/src/test/scala/sttp/client4/impl/zio/SttpClientStubbingTest.scala` (package `sttp.client4.impl.zio`, `AnyFlatSpec with Matchers with ZioTestBase`). Define two top-level test objects in that file: one extending `StreamClientStubbing[Any, Any]` and one extending `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing[Any, Any]`, each overriding `serviceTag` and `sttpBackendTag` with `implicitly` (same pattern as `sttp.client4.httpclient.zio.SttpClientStubbing`). For each: create `Ref.make(obj.backendStub)` with `runtime.unsafeRun`, call `obj.proxy(ref).monad`, assert it is the same instance as `obj.monad` (`should be theSameInstanceAs`), and that it is usable, e.g. `runtime.unsafeRun(m.map(m.unit(1))(_ + 1)) shouldBe 2`. Before the fix the test must fail with StackOverflowError; confirm that by running it once before applying the fix (or reason from the failing run).

Verify: run the new test and the existing zio1 JVM tests on Scala 3 and 2.13, e.g. `sbt "zio1/testOnly sttp.client4.impl.zio.SttpClientStubbingTest"`, `sbt "zio12_13/testOnly sttp.client4.impl.zio.SttpClientStubbingTest"`, then `sbt "zio1/testFull"` and `sbt "zio12_13/testFull"` (confirm the exact project ids with `sbt projects` first). Also compile the dependent `armeria-backend/zio1` project for the same Scala versions. Report actual test output.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules
- `effects/zio1/` — sttp ZIO 1 integration (sbt `projectMatrix` named `zio1` in `build.sbt:545`; JVM + JS, Scala 2.12/2.13/3). Shared sources in `src/main/scala`, JVM-only in `src/main/scalajvm`; tests mirror this (`src/test/scala`, `src/test/scalajvm`, `src/test/scalajs`).
- `effects/zio/` — ZIO 2 integration. Has NO stubbing traits (no `SttpClientStubbingBase.scala`, no `*ClientStubbing`); the bug does not exist there. A repo-wide grep for `def monad ... = monad` matches only the two zio1 lines.
- `armeria-backend/zio1/src/main/scala/sttp/client4/armeria/zio/zio.scala` — the only other user: `object SttpClientStubbing extends StreamClientStubbing[Any, ZioStreams]`. Depends on `zio1`; should still compile.

## File to change
`effects/zio1/src/main/scala/sttp/client4/impl/zio/SttpClientStubbingBase.scala`
- `trait AbstractClientStubbing[R, P]`: `val monad = new RIOMonadAsyncError[R]` (line 20, public, inferred type `RIOMonadAsyncError[R]` — don't change), `protected def backendStub: BackendStub`, `protected def proxy(stub: Ref[BackendStub]): Backend`, `private[sttp] def serviceTag: Tag[Service]`, `private[sttp] def sttpBackendTag: Tag[Backend]`, `val layer: ZLayer[Any, Nothing, Has[Service] & Has[Backend]]`.
- `trait StreamClientStubbing[R, P] extends AbstractClientStubbing[R, P]`: `Backend = StreamBackend[RIO[R, *], P]`, `BackendStub = StreamBackendStub[RIO[R, *], P]`; public `def backendStub` and `def proxy(stub: Ref[StreamBackendStub[RIO[R, *], P]]): StreamBackend[RIO[R, *], P]`. Bug at line 101: `def monad: MonadError[RIO[R, *]] = monad` inside `new StreamBackend[...] { ... }`.
- `trait WebSocketStreamClientStubbing[R, P] extends AbstractClientStubbing[R, P & WebSockets]`: `Backend = WebSocketStreamBackend[RIO[R, *], P]`, `BackendStub = WebSocketStreamBackendStub[RIO[R, *], P]`; public `backendStub` / `proxy`. Same bug at line 120.
- Note `backendStub` and `proxy` are widened to public in the two sub-traits, so a test can call them directly. `layer` is a `val` that needs the tags, evaluated at object init.

## Existing concrete usage (pattern for tags)
`effects/zio1/src/main/scalajvm/sttp/client4/httpclient/zio/package.scala:46`:
```scala
object SttpClientStubbing extends WebSocketStreamClientStubbing[Any, ZioStreams] {
  override private[sttp] def serviceTag: Tag[SttpClientStubbing.Service] = implicitly
  override private[sttp] def sttpBackendTag: Tag[SttpClient.Service] = implicitly
}
```
`HttpClientZioBackend.stubLayer` (`.../httpclient/zio/HttpClientZioBackend.scala:225`) = `SttpClientStubbing.layer`. The zio1 module itself has no concrete `StreamClientStubbing` object (only armeria-zio1 does), so the test must define its own. Tests under package `sttp.client4...` can override the `private[sttp]` members. Define test objects at top level of the file (not nested in the test class) so `Tag` derivation works as in the existing code.

## Tests
- Style: ScalaTest `AnyFlatSpec with Matchers`, mixing in `ZioTestBase` (`effects/zio1/src/test/scala/sttp/client4/impl/zio/ZioTestBase.scala`) which gives `val runtime: Runtime[ZEnv] = Runtime.default`; run effects with `runtime.unsafeRun(...)`. Example: `effects/zio1/src/test/scalajvm/sttp/client4/httpclient/zio/BackendStubZioTests.scala`.
- ZIO 1 API (version 1.0.18): `zio.{Has, RIO, Ref, Tag, Task}`; `Ref.make(a): UIO[Ref[A]]`.
- `sttp.monad.MonadError[F]` has `unit`, `map`, `flatMap`, `error`.
- Stub types are in `sttp.client4.testing` (`StreamBackendStub`, `WebSocketStreamBackendStub`).
- The module uses kind-projector syntax `RIO[R, *]` and `&` / `?` types in cross-compiled sources.

## Build
- sbt 2 with ProjectMatrix. Per `build.sbt:297`: Scala 3 projects have no suffix, Scala 2 ones are suffixed `2_12` / `2_13`; JVM has no platform suffix, JS has `JS`. So expected ids: `zio1` (Scala 3 JVM), `zio12_13`, `zio12_12`, `zio1JS...` — derived from that rule, not run; confirm with `sbt projects`.
- In sbt 2 `test` is incremental; use `testFull` or `testOnly <fqcn>` to force a run. `sbt "testScoped 3 JVM"` runs all JVM Scala 3 projects (too broad here).
- `zio1` has `testServerSettings`: a local test HTTP server starts automatically for the test task.
- Pass multiple sbt commands as one `;`-joined argument (`sbt -batch "a" "b"` was seen running only the first).
- sbt works in this git worktree on current master.
- Do not commit; never add Claude as co-author. Keep comments minimal and non-obvious only.

resultJson.title: Fix infinite recursion in ZIO 1 stubbing proxy `monad`
resultJson.body:
In the ZIO 1 stubbing helpers, the backends created by `StreamClientStubbing.proxy` and `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing.proxy` defined `def monad = monad`. Inside the anonymous class, this called itself, so calling `monad` on the proxied backend caused a `StackOverflowError`. Both now return the outer trait's `RIOMonadAsyncError` via `StreamClientStubbing.this.monad` / `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing.this.monad`.

Added a regression test for both variants. It checks that `monad` is the outer instance and works. The call runs with a 5-second timeout so a regression fails the test instead of hanging. In that case the looping thread keeps running until the JVM exits.

The ZIO 2 module (`effects/zio`) has no stubbing traits, so nothing changed there.
